Zidikai Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Telšiai County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Zidikai's wooden synagogue, built in 1780, was known as the 'cold synagogue' since it was unheated in winter — echoing a similar seasonal naming pattern documented at Vabalninkas elsewhere in this collection. Due to its geographic remoteness, Zidikai's community was notably traditional, and even a modest proposal to replace prayer stands with more comfortable benches sparked years of dispute, resolved only after rabbis from the neighboring towns of Ylakiai, Seda, and Pikeliai — all documented elsewhere in this collection — intervened. In July 1941, the town's men were transferred to Mazeikiai and locked in barns near the Jewish cemetery there, alongside Mazeikiai's own imprisoned Jews; on August 3, they were murdered at that cemetery, and women and children were murdered at the same site six days later.
